newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Business group offers guide to Nazi gold search.
newsitem.headline: Business group offers guide to Nazi gold search.

text.p: The Swiss-American Chamber of Commerce on Friday said it has published a guide to the increasingly complex search for assets of Holocaust victims.
The guide, "Dormant accounts, Nazi gold and loot," offers directions in what has become a labyrinth of major investigations, committees, and task forces.
"The issue of dormant accounts of World War II victims and the Nazi gold issue are overshadowing traditionally excellent Swiss-American relations," said Louis Hughes, president of the Chamber.
The brochure, written by Thomas Maissen, a historian at the University of Potsdam in Germany, aims to give an accurate account of at least the major efforts to date.
-- An independent Swiss expert commission set up according to a decree adopted by Swiss parliament in December.
-- A special task force formed by the Swiss Federal Department of Foreign Affairs led by diplomat Thomas Borer.
-- A central information service set up according to directives of the Swiss Bankers Association (SBA) January 1996, run by banking Ombudsman Hanspeter Haeni.

-- An independent auditing commission headed by former U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Paul Volcker, formed according to a memorandum of understanding signed by the SBA and the World Jewish Restitution Organisation (WJRO) and the World Jewish Congress (WJC).
-- Historical investigations by the WJC into American and foreign archives. U.S. Senate Banking Committee chairman Alfonse D'Amato is also conducting hearings on dormant accounts.
"We try to stick to simply the most important facts and bring transparency to this complex issue," Walter Diggelmann, executive director of the chamber, said.
